history.summary: A large, mature 99-year leasehold mass-market condo in Simei priced at the low absolute entry of $920k with a deep 243-transaction URA series showing 6.1%/yr appreciation. The cheap quantum and strong liquidity are real, but 30 years of age (only ~69 years lease left) and a 1km-plus walk to MRT cap the upside.
history.rating_rationale: PSF $983 sits right at the URA median of $966 (essentially fair value), and 243 transactions confirm a deep buyer pool — this is one of Tampines/Simei's most liquid resale estates with strong HDB-upgrader appeal. The 6.1%/yr URA resale rate is robust on a large sample. But lease decay is now the dominant risk: built 1996, ~69 years remaining, so financing/CPF restrictions begin to bite over a 5-7yr hold and resale buyers will price in further decay. 936 sqft 2BR is generously sized (good livability) but the 1.04km MRT walk and aging facilities limit appreciation versus newer Simei/Tampines stock.
red_flags: Lease ~69 years remaining and falling — CPF/financing haircuts intensify over the hold
1.04km to Upper Changi MRT — not walkable
30-year-old development, dated facilities and higher maintenance
catalysts: Deep HDB-upgrader buyer pool keeps it liquid
Low $920k quantum widens the affordability-driven buyer base
CRL/DTL connectivity improving the wider Tampines region

history.summary: Large 1,313 sqft 3BR in an old (1996, 99yr-from-1992) Simei mass-market condo. Asking $914 psf sits right at the verified market (avg $911-925 psf last 12mo), so the algo's -14.5% cheap signal is mostly a tenure/age artifact, not a true bargain. Good entry quantum and yield, but lease decay caps a 5-7yr investment upside.
history.rating_rationale: Verified URA-backed transactions show Melville Park traded $885-1,080 psf over the last 12 months (avg ~$911-925), so the $914 psf asking is at-market, NOT a -14.5% discount. With ~65yr lease remaining and a 1996 vintage, the unit faces accelerating lease-decay drag over a 5-7yr hold. OCR/D18 region is a forward tailwind (realized fwd OCR ~+4%) and rental yield is solid at 4.1-4.5% on a low quantum, but a large 1,313 sqft floorplate sells at a structurally lower PSF and is the slowest-moving unit type in an old project. Appreciation 6.14% is well-supported (243 txns) but trailing CAGR has ~0 forward power. Fair, liquid, income-friendly, but no clear value edge.

history.summary: A genuinely under-priced unit inside a structurally under-performing project. At $900 psf the ask sits ~6% below Melville Park's own trailing-12-month URA median ($961, 38 resale prints) and ~10% below the identical-size 1,335 sqft unit currently asking $1,335,000 — a real ~$80-130k entry margin, verified against 32 same-size (1,334-1,345 sqft) prints, not a scrape artifact. But the project itself has compounded at only ~2.0%/yr since 2023H1 while D18 resale did ~6.1%/yr and its own Simei old-leasehold neighbours Eastpoint Green and Changi Rise did ~4.4% and ~4.2% — and the 1992 lease (65.1 yrs left, expiry ~Aug 2091) drops through the 60-year line in ~2031, mid-hold. For a 5-7yr resale-profit mandate that is a one-off discount captured at entry, then a laggard with a shortening clock.
history.rating_rationale: PRICE IS RIGHT, VEHICLE IS WRONG. (1) The discount is real and the algo actually understates it: `psf_premium_vs_ura_median_pct` of -1.6% is computed off the 5-year all-time median ($898) in a market up ~7% in 12 months; on the correct trailing-12mo basis ($961) the ask is -6.3%, and it is ~$80-100k under the last five same-size prints ($1,232,500 Oct-25 / $1,320,000 Nov-25 / $1,280,000 Dec-25 / $1,300,000 Mar-26 / $1,290,000 Jun-26). It is also the cheapest live 3BR ask at the project by ~11% (peers $1,009-$1,058 psf). (2) But the algo's biggest positive component, age_value +15.49 on a -21.8% gap to age-adjusted D18 peers, is NOT mean-reversion fuel — it is a structural lease/location discount. Melville Park ($961) and Elias Green ($962, 1991 lease) sit at the floor of D18; the next tier up (Eastpoint Green, same 1996 TOP but a 1996 lease and sited at Simei MRT, $1,158; Changi Rise 2000 lease, $1,154) is ~20% higher, and over 2023H1-2026H1 that gap WIDENED rather than closed (Melville Park 910->966 = +2.0%/yr vs D18 index 1252->1496 = +6.1%/yr). (3) The 6.14% `annual_rate_pct` is a 2021-trough artifact (2021H1 was $707 psf); momentum -0.543 already flags the deceleration. I override forward appreciation to 3.0%/yr. (4) Lease is the decisive variable and it is manageable-but-adverse: 65.1 yrs now, ~58-59 at a 2032-33 exit. Bank tenure is unaffected (a 30yr loan still leaves ~28 yrs), but CPF pro-rating (buyer age + remaining lease must reach 95) moves from biting buyers under 30 today to buyers under ~36-37 at exit — it clips the younger half of the HDB-upgrader pool you would be selling into, and en-bloc offers no offset: no Singapore development above ~1,000 units has ever cleared the 80% consent threshold and this one has 1,232, with no evidence of any collective-sale attempt ever. (5) What holds it at Neutral rather than Avoid: capital is well protected (only one declining half-year median in 5 years, 2023H2->2024H1 at -1.6%), liquidity is genuinely exceptional (243 URA resales in 5 years, ~49/yr on 1,232 units = ~4%/yr turnover, ~49% of buyers coming from HDB addresses), the $1.2M quantum sits in the deepest upgrader band with ~$600k of the $1.8M budget left over, and 4.2-4.5% gross / ~2.5% net yield pays you to wait. At a 3.0%/yr rate plus net carry the 6yr all-in return lands near ~3.5%/yr — an acceptable bond-like hold, not a capital-growth position. (6) VERIFY FIRST: the same unit was cut 11% from $1,350,000 to $1,201,000 in seven weeks on a relist, `floor_level`/`facing` are 0% populated (known broken enricher), there is no stack profile, and the listed sqft moved 1,313 -> 1,335 between listings. An $80-130k below-market ask on an unseen unit is a viewing question, not a finding. This converts to a Buy only if a viewing confirms seller motivation rather than a defect AND the buyer accepts it as a yield/liquidity play.
red_flags: Lease is the decisive variable: 99 yrs from 1 Sep 1992, expiry ~Aug 2091 = 65.1 yrs left; ~58-59 yrs at a 2032-33 exit, so it crosses the 60-year line mid-hold. CPF pro-rating (buyer age + remaining lease >= 95) moves from clipping buyers under 30 today to buyers under ~36-37 at exit, thinning the upgrader pool exactly when you sell.

Project has materially LAGGED, and the gap is widening: URA resale-only half-year medians 2023H1 -> 2026H1 give Melville Park +2.0%/yr vs the D18 resale index +6.1%/yr, Eastpoint Green +4.4%/yr and Changi Rise +4.2%/yr. Its share of the D18 median fell from 72.7% to 64.6%.

The algo's headline signals are both mis-based. `psf_premium_vs_ura_median_pct` -1.6% uses a stale 5-yr median ($898 vs the correct trailing-12mo $961), and the -21.8% vs age-adjusted D18 peers credits a structural lease/location discount as value (the age curve does not control remaining lease). score_1000 790 / valuation 83 are therefore flattering.
6.14% `annual_rate_pct` is a 2021-trough artifact ($707 psf in 2021H1); momentum -0.543. The unmodified ROI table (6.4%/yr) should not be relied on — overridden to 3.0%/yr.

Unverified physical unit: price cut 11% ($1,350,000 -> $1,201,000) in seven weeks on a relist (`relisted_from` 500152749), `floor_level`/`facing` 0% populated, no stack profile, and listed sqft moved 1,313 -> 1,335 between the two listings ($893-$915 psf depending which is right). A second large unit at the project (1,399 sqft, $894 psf) is also asking well under comps - the cheap asks cluster in the slowest-moving large-floorplate band.

No en-bloc / terminal-value optionality: 1,232 units, and no Singapore development above ~1,000 units has cleared the 80% consent threshold. Web research found no evidence of any collective-sale attempt, past or present, and no HIP/SERS/VERS equivalent exists for private leasehold.

30-year-old estate in the cyclical-capex window with split resident sentiment (facilities described as aged and often down, management unresponsive) and a notably LOW verified maintenance fee ($245/mo on a 936 sqft 2BR) - low fees on an ageing 1,232-unit estate raise sinking-fund adequacy / special-levy risk. AGM minutes and sinking-fund balance are not public and must be requested from MCST 2203.

No transit premium: ~960m-1.04km to Upper Changi (DT34) and a disputed 8-14 min walk to Simei (EW3) depending on block. The ~20% PSF gap to MRT-adjacent Eastpoint Green is largely the price of that walk.

DTL3 Extension is NOT a catalyst for this address despite how it is marketed: Xilin (DT36, opening 2H2026) sits at 301 Xilin Avenue serving Changi South industrial and is not walkable from Simei Street 1 - the repo's 1,011m figure looks optimistic. Repo priors also give the future-infrastructure score no measured forward power.

Exit-window supply: the 2029-2031 TOP wave (Parktown Residence 1,193 units at a benchmark ~$2,360 psf, Pinery Residences ~585, plus Bedok Rise and Bayshore Drive GLS ~2,300) lands on a 2031-2033 exit and pulls the trade-up cohort, even though it is a different price tier.

REALSCORE and realsmart profitability stats are UNAVAILABLE - the cached realsmart record for melville-park resolved but returned null for realscore, pct_profitable, resale_txns and annual_return_pct. Per instructions it was not re-fetched, so the usual downside cross-check is missing and was substituted with the URA half-year median series.
catalysts: Genuine entry margin, verified against a deep cohort: $900 psf vs the project's $961 trailing-12mo median (38 URA resale prints) and vs 32 same-size 1,334-1,345 sqft prints; ~$80-100k below the last five same-size done deals and ~10% below the identical 1,335 sqft unit currently asking $1,335,000. Cheapest live 3BR ask at the project by ~11%.

Exceptional exit liquidity for old OCR stock: 243 URA resales in 5 years (~49/yr on 1,232 units, ~4%/yr turnover), ~49% of buyers arriving from HDB addresses and ~56% Singaporean - a genuinely deep, financing-insensitive local upgrader bid.
Low quantum in the deepest buyer band: $1.2M leaves ~$600k of the ~$1.8M budget unspent, and OCR carries the repo's strongest realized forward regional return (+3.7%/yr vs RCR +3.1%, CCR +1.9%).

Real positive carry: rent $4,200/mo per URA project+bed data (confidence 0.95), and web evidence is firmer still - $3.47 psf/mo project average and a 1,346 sqft 3BR asking $4,500/mo imply ~$4,400-4,600 for this unit, i.e. 4.2-4.5% gross and ~2.5% net.
Downside is well evidenced: only one declining half-year median in eleven half-years since 2021 (2023H2 $914 -> 2024H1 $899, -1.6%), and the same-size band still printed $958-988 psf in Jun 2026.

Vintage is not automatically a drag: Stacked Homes (May 2025) finds 1980s-90s condos annualised ~3.2%, matching or beating newer stock - which is why the forward override is 3.0%/yr rather than the 2.0% three-year run-rate.

Near-term East supply is tight (ERA, Nov 2025: only ~1,100 private + ~1,320 EC units launching in the East in 2026), which supports resale pricing into 2027-2028 before the 2029-2031 completion wave arrives.

agent_evaluation.rental_assessment: Solid and the strongest part of the case. URA project+bed data puts a 3BR here at $4,200/mo (confidence 0.95) = 4.2% gross / 2.47% net; independent web evidence is slightly better ($3.47 psf/mo project average, a 1,346 sqft 3BR asking $4,500/mo), implying ~$4,400-4,600 and 4.4-4.6% gross for this unit. Demand drivers are durable rather than speculative: Changi Business Park, SUTD, ITE College East, Changi General Hospital and Changi Airport within a short commute, plus Simei/Eastpoint Mall amenity. Large 1,335 sqft 3BRs rent to families and sharers at a lower psf than the project's small units, so expect the rent to be at the project average, not above it. Carry is positive and pays you to hold, which is the main reason this is a Neutral rather than an Avoid.

The data rate of 6.14%/yr (243 txns) is a 2021-trough artifact - the project's half-year median PSF ran $707 (2021H1) -> $910 (2023H1) in the post-COVID recovery, then almost stalled: $910 -> $914 -> $899 -> $907 -> $920 -> $956 -> $966 (2026H1). That is +2.0%/yr over the last three years, against a D18 resale index that did +6.1%/yr over the identical window, and against Simei old-leasehold neighbours Eastpoint Green (+4.4%/yr) and Changi Rise (+4.2%/yr). The two-year run-rate is better (+3.7%/yr) and Jun-2026 prints ($958-988 psf on 1,302-1,345 sqft) show the recent firmness is real, so the honest forward anchor is roughly the OCR baseline shaded down for lease decay: I override to 3.0%/yr. Over a 5-7yr hold the lease goes 65 -> 58 years, crossing the 60-year threshold at which commentary and CPF mechanics both agree the discount steepens, and there is no en-bloc offset at 1,232 units. Expect the entry discount to be the bulk of the profit, not the compounding.
agent_evaluation.stack_notes: Not researchable from available data - and this is the single largest gap. No profile exists for Melville Park (`stack_profile.status = not_researched`), `floor_level` and `facing` are 0% populated across the DB (known broken enricher), and web research found no credible stack/facing ranking. Known: 9 blocks at 12-28 Simei Street 1 (even numbers), 52 floor-plan types spanning 936-1,561 sqft, 2BR and 3BR only, units facing north-west, south-east or the internal courtyard; secondary sources claim a 3-5% corner-unit premium (unverified). Transaction records show sales in an 11-15 floor band despite sources describing blocks as 'up to 11 storeys' - unresolved. Notably, this project is NOT strongly floor-stratified: recent 01-05 floor prints ($1,017-1,032 psf in Jan-Feb 2026) match or beat 06-10 prints, so a low floor alone does not explain a $900 psf ask. This unit is at 20 Simei Street 1. Walk time to Simei MRT varies 8-14 min by block across the ~7.5ha site - verify on foot for block 20 specifically. The PIE lies to the north; north-facing low floors are the obvious noise suspects, but that is inference, not evidence. A viewing must establish floor, facing, renovation state and any road/carpark exposure before the discount can be credited.
agent_evaluation.appreciation_rate_source: Resale-to-resale only. Melville Park's own URA resale half-year median PSF: 2023H1 $910 -> 2026H1 $966 = +2.0%/yr (3yr); 2024H1 $899 -> 2026H1 $966 = +3.7%/yr (2yr). Simei old-leasehold peers over the same 3yr window: Eastpoint Green +4.4%/yr, Changi Rise +4.2%/yr; D18 resale index +6.1%/yr. Cross-checked against Stacked Homes (May 2025) finding 1980s-90s vintage condos annualise ~3.2%. Set at 3.0%/yr: above the project's 3yr run-rate given firm Jun-2026 prints ($958-988 psf), but below the OCR +3.7% regional baseline because the lease crosses 60 years in ~2031, mid-hold. The 6.14% data rate is rejected as a 2021-trough artifact (momentum -0.543).
